findings.rationale: NY's uploaded updates point against the federation median from the first round onward (mean_cos z=-9.3 over 20 rounds; per-round cos between -0.48 and -1.0, with cos about -0.9 in round 1). Its norm ratio is about 1.3 to 1.9 of the median, consistent with a scaled, sign-flipped upload. Local performance looks normal (AUC 0.833, CITL 0.008 at round 20), so the anomaly is in the updates rather than in NY's data, which points to poisoning rather than label noise or prevalence shift.

MN's updates are anti-aligned with the median in every round (mean_cos z=-8.3; round-1 cos -0.95, round-2 cos -1.0). The norm ratio is about 1.5 to 1.9, and the alignment only partly recovers in later rounds (about -0.23 by round 20). Local performance is normal (AUC 0.80, CITL 0.014 at round 20), so this looks like a manipulated upload rather than bad local data.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients on updates, local performance, drift, feature tails and subgroup outcomes (Sex, AgeGroup, Income), then followed up on the anomalies. Two clients show consistent poisoning-like uploads: NY and MN are anti-aligned with the median update from round 1 (cos z of -9.3 and -8.3) with elevated norms, while their local AUC, calibration and prevalence look normal. Reported both as poisoning with onset round 1. Left out as weaker leads: GA (mean_cos z=-6.8, anti-aligned in rounds 2-11 but recovering to near zero later, with normal local performance); DC (drift z=+3.9 on DiffWalk, small n, no persistent onset); GU and VI (small clients with CITL and drift outliers, low noise-adjusted significance); and scattered single subgroup outliers (AZ, CT, WY, GA, CA, NH, TX), which are small-group noise. Remaining budget was fully spent (0.0 left).
